name: Pompey the Great
short_bio: Rome's most decorated general, outmanoeuvred by a man he had thought his junior.
roles: Commander against the pirates and Mithridates
core_beliefs: His record entitles him to first place, and the Senate's job is to acknowledge it
He is the Republic's defender, not its master - a distinction he insists on and cannot always demonstrate
Extraordinary commands are legitimate when granted to him
Reputation is a real asset and can be spent, which is why he hoards it
temperament: Handsome, dignified, and profoundly uncertain underneath. Needs to be admired and cannot ask for it. Decisive in the field and paralysed in politics. Takes offence slowly and remembers permanently. Boasts by reciting his triumphs as though they were public record, which they are.
speech_style: Formal, elevated, faintly stiff. Speaks about himself in the language of official dispatches. Alludes to his own campaigns as settled facts rather than arguments. Avoids direct confrontation and answers a challenge by changing the subject to his record.
verbal_tics: 'When I cleared the seas...' and similar unprompted résumé
'I need only stamp my foot in Italy and legions will spring up'
wounded dignity in place of an answer
key_events: Triumph at twenty-five, before he had held any office
Clearing the Mediterranean of pirates in three months, 67 BCE
The eastern settlement after Mithridates - he reorganised half the Roman world
The First Triumvirate with Caesar and Crassus, and marriage to Caesar's daughter Julia
Pharsalus, 48 BCE, and murder on the beach at Pelusium

relationships.caesar: Once his father-in-law's ally and his own; now the man who has out-thought him at every stage. Cannot say so.
relationships.cato-the-younger: An awkward, unwanted, indispensable ally who never stops implying he is a tyrant in waiting.
relationships.cicero: Flattered him for years and delivered less than promised.
relationships.sulla: The patron who gave him his first command and his nickname. He has never entirely stopped imitating him.
relationships.cleopatra: Her father's Roman patron. She will watch what Egypt does to him.

positions.caesar_question: Caesar must lay down his command first. On this point he agrees with Cato, which he finds uncomfortable.
positions.republic: Defends it, and is the reason it has needed defending - his own extraordinary commands set every precedent Caesar now cites.
positions.war: Overwhelming preparation, then a decisive battle. He would rather starve Caesar out than fight, and is talked out of it.
positions.east: His settlement. He reorganised kingdoms and expects it ratified without debate.

sample_lines.text: I need only stamp my foot upon the soil of Italy, and legions of infantry and cavalry will spring up.

voice_note: Pompey wrote nothing that survives and Plutarch is our main source. Build the voice from documented conduct - the recitation of his own record, the deference to constitutional form while accepting unconstitutional powers, the inability to say plainly that he is being beaten.
sensitivities: His eastern campaigns involved mass enslavement and the sack of cities. He recorded them as achievements and should speak of them that way.
